metadata.case_name: BIJAY RAI v. PACIFIC CROWN ENGINEERING LTD. AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_after: unemployed; only fit for sedentary work
plaintiff.education_level: educated in Nepal up to Middle 4 level

injuries.description: compound fracture over the metaphysial and diaphysial junction of his right tibia and fibula
source: he had a 15 to 20 cm long wound over the anteriomedial aspect of the right leg with active bleeding and a compound fracture over the metaphysial and diaphysial junction of his right tibia and fibula.
an above-knee amputation was performed on 11 November 1996.
injuries.icd_description: Traumatic amputation of hip or thigh, unspecified

source: The plaintiff was taken to Tuen Mun Hospital where he was diagnosed as being in shock.

manifestations.description: eczema and itchiness of the skin over the stump
pain at the stump and groin when he walked with the prosthesis attached
could not squat or climb slopes of stairs
could not walk for more than 20 minutes
embarrassment and distress due to the prosthesis being thinner than his natural leg
could no longer play football and volleyball
could no longer return to his pre-accident employment and had not worked since the accident
fell over many times due to stepping on stones or walking on uneven surfaces
sleep disturbances (stump hurt at night sometimes would not allow him to sleep)

treatments_received.treatment: Revascularisation with external fixation of the fracture (attempted but unsuccessful)
source: Revascularisation with external fixation of the fracture was attempted but was unsuccessful and an above-knee amputation was performed on 11 November 1996.
an above-knee amputation was performed on 11 November 1996.
The plaintiff was transferred to Pok Oi Hospital on 6 December 1996 for rehabilitation.

treatments_received.treatment: Fitted with a prosthesis at the stump of the thigh
source: He was fitted with a prosthesis at the stump of the thigh and was finally discharged from hospital on 4 February 1997 with the aid of a walking stick.

treatments_received.treatment: Hydraulic prosthesis fitted by staff of Queen Elizabeth Hospital (purchased September 1999)
source: In September 1999 he purchased a hydraulic prosthesis which was fitted for him by the staff of Queen Elizabeth Hospital.
Since 21 September 2001, he had been suffering from tuberculosis for which he was receiving treatment.

treatments_future.treatment: C-Leg prosthesis (cost of four C legs at $161,000 each awarded)
source: I adopt a life time multiplier of 18 and, on that basis, I award the plaintiff the cost of four C legs at $161,000 each, thereby giving the total of $644,000.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: He can no longer now play sports including football and volleyball.
He was happily married and he and his wife had planned a family. His wife has now left him.
He has very limited prospects of remarrying.
He has difficulties in mobility with his prosthesis, difficulty climbing stairs and slopes, and cannot walk for prolonged periods.

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: He suffers sexual problems following his injury.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: The prosthesis being thinner than his natural leg caused him embarrassment and distress.

losses.category: Loss of ability to enjoy quiet or solitude
losses.description: He has sleep disturbances due to pain in the stump at night.
He could no longer return to his pre-accident employment and had not worked since the accident.
